requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to put each new or changed requirement into a group, where a group holds requirements that cite each other or describe one feature. It MUST direct them to review every group with its own read-only subagent, with all the reviews running in parallel, before presenting any group to the user.
rationale:
The subject constrains the text of the bundled `habeas-requirements` skill. It requires four things:
- The skill directs agents to put each new or changed requirement into a group.
- A group holds requirements that cite each other or describe one feature.
- The skill directs a review of every group by its own read-only subagent, with all reviews in parallel.
- That review happens before any group is presented to the user.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_reviews_each_group_with_a_parallel_read_only_subagent]` is the only test marked `{test}`. It checks each obligation:
- It uses `step_of(SKILL, "start a read-only subagent")` to find the workflow step that mentions a read-only subagent. It panics if no step has that phrase, so the skill must direct a read-only subagent.
- It runs `assert_text` on that step's collapsed text for three phrases.
  - "Sort the new and changed requirements into groups" covers grouping each new or changed requirement.
  - "requirements that cite each other or describe one feature" covers the group definition.
  - "For each group, start a read-only subagent, all in parallel" covers one subagent per group, read-only, and parallel.
- It asserts `review < step_of(SKILL, "Present each group to the user")`. That covers the review happening before any group is presented.

The helpers `workflow_steps`, `step`, `step_of` and `assert_text` collapse whitespace, so they handle the skill's line-wrapped Markdown. They assert phrase containment and fail with messages. They also cover the case where the review step is missing or the wrong step is picked.

The skill step in `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` (Workflow step 3) contains these phrases. The test is a text-presence check of a document, which is the only way to test a requirement about what a skill directs. No obligation is untested, and nothing in the subject is ambiguous or acknowledged by a `{fixme}`.
